title: Neonatal and paediatric reference values (vitals, CSF, haematology, chemistry)
_comment: Row: { analyte, when, lo?, hi?, median?, centiles?, mean?, sd?, range_min?, range_max?, unit, note, src, quote }. 'when' keys: ga_wk, pna_d, dol, hours, age_months, age_years ({min,gt,max,lt}); at_birth:true marks the immediate neonatal period. A range condition may carry its own src+quote when its number comes from a different sentence of the same source (e.g. the preterm definition). lo/hi meaning differs by source; read 'note'. Values are copied as published, never converted.

groups.title: Neonatal chemistry: glucose operational thresholds (BAPM 2024) and term day 1 to 3 serum calcium, magnesium, sodium, potassium

rows.note: BAPM 2024 framework scope: full-term infant, birth to 72 hours. Operational threshold for intervention, not a normal range: act if BG is below lo. Any baby, a single value below 1.0.
rows.quote: 6. An operational threshold approach should be used to guide interventions intended to raise BG: • A value <1.0mmol/L at any time • A single value <2.5mmol/L in a neonate with abnormal clinical signs • More than two measurements <2.0mmol/L in a baby with a risk factor for impaired metabolic adaptation and hypoglycaemia but without abnormal clinical signs

rows.analyte: Blood glucose operational threshold (abnormal clinical signs)
rows.note: BAPM 2024 framework scope: full-term infant, birth to 72 hours. Operational threshold for intervention, not a normal range: act if BG is below lo. Single value below 2.5 with abnormal clinical signs.
rows.quote: 6. An operational threshold approach should be used to guide interventions intended to raise BG: • A value <1.0mmol/L at any time • A single value <2.5mmol/L in a neonate with abnormal clinical signs • More than two measurements <2.0mmol/L in a baby with a risk factor for impaired metabolic adaptation and hypoglycaemia but without abnormal clinical signs

rows.analyte: Blood glucose operational threshold (risk factor, no abnormal signs)
rows.note: BAPM 2024 framework scope: full-term infant, birth to 72 hours. Operational threshold for intervention, not a normal range: act if BG is below lo. Practice Point 6 wording: more than two measurements below 2.0. The framework's evidence section words the same threshold as '<2.0mmol/L and remaining <2.0mmol/L at next measurement'; see ambiguity.
rows.quote: 6. An operational threshold approach should be used to guide interventions intended to raise BG: • A value <1.0mmol/L at any time • A single value <2.5mmol/L in a neonate with abnormal clinical signs • More than two measurements <2.0mmol/L in a baby with a risk factor for impaired metabolic adaptation and hypoglycaemia but without abnormal clinical signs

rows.analyte: Blood glucose target (suspected or confirmed hyperinsulinism)
rows.note: BAPM 2024 Practice Point 25: maintain BG above lo. The evidence section states '3.5mmol/L after 72 hours of age' for the later threshold; see ambiguity.
rows.quote: aim to maintain BG concentration >3.0mmol/L in the first 48 hours and >3.5mmol/L after 48 hours from birth.

rows.analyte: Blood glucose target (suspected or confirmed hyperinsulinism)
rows.note: BAPM 2024 Practice Point 25: maintain BG above lo.
rows.quote: aim to maintain BG concentration >3.0mmol/L in the first 48 hours and >3.5mmol/L after 48 hours from birth.

rows.note: BAPM 2024: at least this value in moderate-severe HIE.
rows.quote: The operational threshold should be increased to at least 2.5mmol/L in infants with moderate-severe hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy
